notes:
I couldn't write these notes. My first attempt to fetch the sources (Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary, Barnes and Wesley on biblehub.com, and the NET Bible notes) hit the tool-use limit, and the retry was blocked. I didn't read any page from the allowed sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point, and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I have no sources, I've left out all verse notes rather than write content you can't check.

When the tools are available again, these are the pages I'd read first:

**1. Traditional verse-by-verse reading**
- https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/job-24/
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/job/24.htm
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/job/24.htm
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/job/24.htm
- https://biblehub.com/commentaries/barnes/job/24.htm
- Precept Austin's Job 24 page on preceptaustin.org

**2. Differences between Protestant traditions**
- Methodist: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wesley/job/24.htm, and Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu
- Reformed: Ligonier and Monergism
- Baptist: Spurgeon and Desiring God
- Lutheran: 1517.org and lcms.org
- Pentecostal: pneumareview.com
- Anglican: Ryle and the Anglican commentaries on studylight.org

**3. Other views**
- Translation notes: https://netbible.org/bible/Job+24, which matter most for the hard verses 12 and 18–24
- Modern scholarship: bibleodyssey.org
- Catholic: newadvent.org, which has the Church Fathers, including Gregory the Great's *Moralia on Job*
- Orthodox: oca.org

One open question for the research: many commentators believe verses 18–24 may not be Job's own view. They may be quoting his friends, or the text may have been moved. The sources will need to show how each one handles that, because it changes how those verses are read.

You can ask again in a new message, or I can start with a smaller batch, such as verses 1–12 from Enduring Word and Ellicott alone.
